clue.text: Batting position, for example

parts.note: a batsman who is batting is said to be in
a stance is the position a player takes up

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator offers the batsman's stance as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batting position' reads as a single cricket phrase, but it splits in two; 'for' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a case or illustration, i.e. an example of something.

clue.text: Animal captured in Blenheim Palace

indicators.note: the animal is held prisoner within the run of letters of the palace's name

explanation.surface: A creature has been caught inside the grand Oxfordshire stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: Blenheim Palace is a stately home in Oxfordshire, England; the answer sits across its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is a graceful African antelope, a species of animal.

clue.text: Dog merely tears hair out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A distressed owner is simply pulling out hair in frustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of the phrase 'tears hair out' but signals the anagram of all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sealyham terrier is a small white Welsh breed of hunting dog.

clue.text: Wine bar finally moving

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word bar

explanation.surface: The wine bar is at last getting going.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in motion, stirring.

clue.text: Cézanne's first borders take on vivid colour

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the painter's name

parts.note: rims are the borders or edges of things
to take someone on is to accept their challenge, as in 'you're on'

explanation.surface: The painter's first picture has edges that take on a vivid colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan text lost the opening letters of Cézanne; the painter supplies only his initial C.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep vivid red shade.

clue.text: Heartless rabbit is Pythonesque primarily a monster

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the rabbit word is removed

parts.note: bunny is a child's word for a rabbit

indicators.note: primarily takes the opening letter of each of the two words is and Pythonesque

explanation.surface: A rabbit with no heart sounds like a Monty Python monster.
explanation.walkthrough: A bunyip is a monster of Australian Aboriginal legend; 'Heartless' takes one N from the middle of BUNNY.
explanation.definitionFit: The bunyip is a mythical swamp-dwelling creature from Australian folklore.

clue.text: Ivan's rule is terrible in Hollywood studios

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters are in a dreadful mess, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: The rule of Ivan the Terrible is described as terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ivan' and 'terrible' together evoke the Russian tsar, but 'is terrible' is the anagram signal for the nine letters of IVAN'S RULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal is one of the major film production companies based in Hollywood.

clue.text: It's impossible to predict the effect of the Official Secrets Act

definitions.text: the effect of the Official Secrets Act

explanation.surface: The consequences of state secrecy laws cannot be foreseen.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the outcome cannot be foreseen; read literally it says secrets law bars you from ever telling.

clue.text: Agreeable Spanish saint enters the fold

indicators.note: enters means one word goes inside another

parts.note: a pleat is a fold in cloth
San is the Spanish word for saint, as in San Diego

explanation.surface: A Spanish saint walks into the sheepfold, pleasingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fold' suggests a sheep pen or church congregation, but it is a pleat in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant means nice and agreeable to be with.

clue.text: Insect found in ordinary fruit

indicators.note: found in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: plain means ordinary, unadorned
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug has turned up in a piece of everyday fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The plantain is a starchy banana-like fruit cooked as a staple.

clue.text: Very small sort of steak? Make a note of it

explanation.surface: A tiny steak is worth jotting down.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny is one sense; a thin quick-fried cut is a steak type; to minute something is to record it formally.

clue.text: Formerly head has expelled blockhead

indicators.note: has expelled means a letter is thrown out of the word for head

parts.note: bonce is British slang for the head
the head of the word block is its first letter, B

explanation.surface: A headteacher has thrown out a dim pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blockhead' looks like an insult for a fool; read as 'block's head' it is the letter B. BONCE is British slang for head.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at one time in the past, i.e. previously.

clue.text: Film set seen by monarch

parts.note: to set something down is to lay it
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A film set is visited by the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film set' reads as a movie studio; 'Film' is a thin coating and 'set' gives LAY. 'seen by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer is a thin coating or sheet, like a film on a surface.

clue.text: It's foolish to feel inferior

parts.note: to sense something is to feel it
less means lower in rank or inferior

explanation.surface: Feeling inferior is a silly thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Senseless means lacking good sense, stupid or pointless.

clue.text: Virgin soldiers accept support

indicators.note: accept means the soldiers take another word inside them

parts.note: men are ordinary soldiers, the ranks
aid means help or support

explanation.surface: Inexperienced troops take on help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin soldiers' recalls the novel and film title, but 'Virgin' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is an unmarried girl, traditionally a virgin.

clue.text: Appear casual for lecture

explanation.surface: Dressing informally to give a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress down is both to wear informal clothes and to scold someone severely.

clue.text: European leader back from the orient

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the word European

parts.note: astern means at or towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A European leader returns from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern describes things coming from or relating to the East, i.e. Asian lands.

clue.text: Foot fault for a peasant

indicators.note: fault suggests the letters are defective and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A foot fault in tennis called against a farm labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot fault' is a tennis term, but 'Foot' is a metrical unit and 'fault' signals the anagram; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An anapaest is a metrical foot of two short syllables then one long.

clue.text: Maniacs, say, going in opposite directions

indicators.note: going in means one word is placed inside another

parts.note: N and S, north and south, are opposite compass directions
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Madmen are speaking while heading in opposite directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutters is British slang for crazy people, lunatics.

clue.text: Small book by Kipling may be read superficially

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Kim is a novel by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: A short Kipling book may be skimmed rather than studied.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim a text is to glance through it quickly without close reading.

clue.text: Spite in country cottage that's been vacated

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: a vacated word has been emptied, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Spiteful feeling lingers in an abandoned country cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country cottage' reads as one phrase, but 'country' is Mali and 'cottage' is emptied to CE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to harm others, ill will.

clue.text: Start to mark spy with a dye

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the word mark

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: A spy begins marking with a dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red aniline dye, named after an Italian battle.

clue.text: Mischief-maker may be holy

explanation.surface: A troublemaker might also be considered saintly.
explanation.definitionFit: A terror is a naughty child; the idiom 'holy terror' describes such a nuisance.

clue.text: Dying general captures island

indicators.note: captures means the general's name takes a letter inside it

parts.note: John Pershing was the US general commanding in the First World War

explanation.surface: A dying general seizes an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Perishing means dying or passing away; also used for bitterly cold.

clue.text: Weapon for knight leaving a lot to be desired?

indicators.note: leaving means the following words are left off the knight's name
to be desired completes the idiom and marks the words as missing

parts.note: Lancelot is the Arthurian knight of the Round Table
a lot is read as the letters of LOT, sounding like the end of the knight's name

explanation.surface: A knight's weapon is decidedly unsatisfactory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving a lot to be desired' is an idiom for poor quality, but it literally removes LOT from Lancelot.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by mounted knights.

clue.text: Drop bricks around West End

indicators.note: around means the toy bricks surround another letter

parts.note: Lego is a brand of toy building bricks

indicators.note: End means the final letter of the word West

explanation.surface: Bricks are dropped around London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London's theatre district but gives T, the end of West.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go of something is to release or drop it.

clue.text: Backing team working for recording pioneer

indicators.note: backing means the word for team is read backwards

parts.note: a side is a sports team
on means working, switched on

explanation.surface: A supporting team is working for a pioneer of sound recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison invented the phonograph, the first device to record and replay sound.

clue.text: King taking a winter break in cast-off clothing?

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

indicators.note: break means the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A king takes a winter holiday wearing hand-me-down clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winter break' reads as a holiday, but 'break' rearranges A WINTER; 'cast-off' is the knitting term for finishing, not discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitted garments are finished by casting off stitches, hence jumpers and cardigans.

clue.text: County seen on entering ancient port

indicators.note: entering means one word goes inside another

parts.note: Tyre was an ancient Phoenician port in Lebanon

explanation.surface: A county is seen while entering an old harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: TYRONE is a county in Northern Ireland; 'seen' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrone is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: One singing bird to follow about

indicators.note: to follow means the bird is placed after the other piece

parts.note: ca is the abbreviation of circa, meaning about
the roller is a colourful bird that tumbles in flight

explanation.surface: A songbird is told to follow someone around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One singing bird' reads as a songbird, but 'bird' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A caroller sings Christmas songs door to door.
